newsitem.title: USA: TU keeps Comanche Peak 2 at reduced output.
newsitem.headline: TU keeps Comanche Peak 2 at reduced output.

text.p: Texas Utilities Co said Monday it expects to keep its 1,150 megawatt (MW) Comanche Peak 2 nuclear power unit at reduced output for additional repairs.
The unit is currently producing power at 55 percent of capacity, said company spokeswoman Pat Nichols.
"It's probably not going to go above that level for most of the week," she said.
When the unit reached 60 percent power Sunday, plant crews detected problems at a heater drain pump and one of its feedwater pumps, Nichols said.
A heater drain pump helps collect condensed steam and a feedwater pump circulates water for steam production.
The unit tripped off line Wednesday Sept 18 after a lightning storm knocked out a feed water pump.
The adjoining Comanche Peak 1, also at 1,150 MW, continued to generate electricity at full output, she said.
The Comanche Peak units, in Glen Rose, Tx., produce about 18 percent of the company's electricity deliveries.
Texas Utilities is the operator and sole owner of the Comanche Peak facility.
